chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Abu al-Jahm, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Ahmad ibn Sulayman, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said:
The miser is the one who is miserly with what Allah has Obligated upon him.
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of a miser in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this concise definition from al-Kafi, Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) reorients the concept of stinginess from a general character flaw to a specific failure in fulfilling divine obligations, such as Zakat and Khums. This aligns with Shia juristic emphasis on the spiritual consequences of neglecting mandatory dues, framing miserliness as a breach of covenant with Allah rather than merely a social vice.
